blocks.text: ASAPH THE SINGER, CALLED “THE SEER” (2 CHRONICLES 29:30) · UNITED KINGDOM
Asaph. Chief of the singers before the ark; twelve psalms bear his name.
SCRIPTURE CALLS
Prophesied with harps
ERA
United kingdom c. 1050–930 BC
IN THE DAYS OF
David · Solomon
BOOK
None bears the name
HOW THE WORD CAME
He led with cymbals: “Asaph made a sound with cymbals”.
THE CALL
How the word came
He led with cymbals: “Asaph made a sound with cymbals”. 1 Chronicles 15:19 1 Chronicles 16:5
His sons were “under the hands of Asaph, which prophesied according to the order of the king”. 1 Chronicles 25:2
Chronicles calls him “Asaph the seer”, and Hezekiah's Levites sang “the words of David, and of Asaph”. 2 Chronicles 29:30

From the textTwelve psalms carry his name in their titles: Psalm 50 and Psalms 73 to 83 (for example “A Psalm of Asaph”). The titles do not say when the psalms were written. Psalms 50:1 Psalms 73:1 Psalms 74:1 Psalms 75:1 Psalms 76:1 Psalms 77:1 +6 more
BEFORE THE KINGS
Before two kings
KING OF JUDAH, THEN OF ALL ISRAEL
David
“Then on that day David delivered first this psalm to thank the LORD into the hand of Asaph and his brethren.”
1 Chronicles 16:7 (KJV) →
KING OF ALL ISRAEL
Solomon
THE SONGS
What he sang
Thanks before the ark
“Give thanks unto the LORD, call upon his name, make known his deeds among the people.”
1 Chronicles 16:8 (KJV) →
Songs remembered after the exile
“For in the days of David and Asaph of old there were chief of the singers, and songs of praise and thanksgiving unto God.”
Nehemiah 12:46 (KJV) →
PLACES
Where his story happened
Jerusalem · Before the ark in the tent David pitched for it
SIGNS
Signs and wonders
WONDER
The cloud at the temple's dedication
COMPANIONS AND OPPONENTS
Who stood with him, and against him
Heman
Jeduthun
Berachiah, his father
Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah and Asarelah, his sons
Jahaziel, “of the sons of Asaph”
HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS

From the textScripture does not tell of Asaph's death. His line went on: Jahaziel, “a Levite of the sons of Asaph”, prophesied before Jehoshaphat; Hezekiah's Levites sang “the words of David, and of Asaph the seer”; at Josiah's passover “the singers the sons of Asaph were in their place”; and “the children of Asaph” are named among the singers who came back from the exile. 2 Chronicles 20:14 2 Chronicles 29:30 2 Chronicles 35:15 Ezra 2:41 Nehemiah 7:44
TRADITION SAYS
No tradition is recorded here.
OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
Asaph, David's singer
The titles as they stand; the Pulpit Commentary (1880–1897) on Psalm 73

Hezekiah's Levites sang “the words of David, and of Asaph the seer”. The Pulpit Commentary notes that “the triumph of Absalom” has been suggested as the occasion of Psalm 73. 2 Chronicles 29:30 Psalms 73:1 [101]
Later singers of Asaph's line or guild, for some of them
R. Jamieson, A. R. Fausset and D. Brown (1871); A. F. Kirkpatrick (1895); M. Jastrow Jr. and others, Jewish Encyclopedia (1902)

Psalm 74 laments a sanctuary burned and cast down. If that is the Babylonian conquest, JFB says the author was “probably a descendant and namesake” of Asaph; Kirkpatrick weighs Shishak's raid, the Babylonian conquest and the Maccabean age, and says that apart from the title “all other considerations are against” Shishak. The Jewish Encyclopedia calls Asaph the “Eponym of a musical gild”. Psalms 74:1 Psalms 74:7 [56][70][42]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
1 Chronicles 16:7 says David delivered the psalm into Asaph's hand; it does not say Asaph wrote it.
Scripture does not say when the psalms of Asaph were written.
Other men named Asaph are different people: the father of Joah the recorder (2 Kings 18:18) and the keeper of the king's forest (Nehemiah 2:8).
